O.outcome_detail: intubation success on a difficult-airway manikin

cells.quote: Ambrosio et al. conducted a randomized trial comparing DL and GVL intubation performance on a difficult airway manikin among novice physicians with little to no prior intubation experience.7 These novice physicians had 47.4% success with DL and 100% success with GVL.
cells.note: The study text reports success percentages but does not report an inferential test or confidence interval for the difference.

O.outcome_detail: endotracheal intubation success in stable patients

cells.quote: Nouruzi-Sedeh et al. also compared the success of DL to GVL in untrained medical personnel performing intubations on stable patients in the operating room.8 They found that these novices had success of only 51% with DL but 90% with GVL.
cells.note: The study text reports success percentages but does not state random assignment, duration, or an inferential test.

cells.quote: However, in the model for GVL, first pass success for PGY-2 and PGY-3 residents improved compared to PGY-1 residents (PGY-2 aOR 2.1, 95% CI 1.1–3.8, p-value 0.021; PGY-3 aOR 4.1, 95% CI 2.1–8.0, p<0.001) (Table 2b).
cells.note: Retrospective observational analysis; the model adjusted for reason for intubation, difficult airway characteristics, calendar year, and resident as a mixed effect.

cells.note: Calendar year was included as a possible confounder in the logistic mixed-effects model.
